# Task Instruction

You handle estimating at a parking systems integrator in Qingdao. A colleague spent this morning at a residential compound scoping an entrance barrier and plate recognition job. What came back is in `materials/`: two photographs of the entrances, and a photograph of the sheet he wrote while he was on site.

Turn that into the formal quotation we issue to the customer. Save it as an Excel workbook at `output/quotation.xlsx`.

The customer reads this document to decide whether to sign, and our own installers work from it once the job starts, so it has to stand on its own after the scoping sheet is no longer attached to it. The sheet is our record of what the site needs.

House rules that apply to every quotation we issue:

1. Unit prices are the ones settled on site.
2. We do not bill installation to the customer as a lump sum. Transport and commissioning is charged at 10 percent, maintenance at another 10 percent, both calculated on the total of everything quoted before those two charges.
3. Our prices are inclusive of a general VAT invoice at 1 percent.
4. Date the quotation 2026.7.21.

We move quantities around during negotiation, so the line amounts and the totals need to recalculate inside the workbook rather than sit there as typed in numbers.
grouping_policy: Location/work-package/trade-based groupings are all acceptable. No private reference taxonomy. Subtotals or a formula total over all quoted lines are accepted. Photographs establish entrances, not measured cable lengths.
site_works_policy:
# Site works takeoff from a round figure

Use this when the survey record gives cabling, containment or civil work as a single figure.

## Why a round figure is hard to quote

A single figure hides how far things run, what each run needs, and what a unit of work costs. The customer cannot test it and the crew cannot build to it, and when the site differs from the survey there is no agreed way to adjust it.

## Taking it apart

1. From the photographs and notes, identify what the figure physically pays for: the kinds of cable, the containment they run in, any work to surfaces or structures they cross, and any bases or fixings.
2. Estimate each quantity from the layout: where things start and end, how many runs, and a sensible allowance for routing. Record the basis of each estimate in terms of the site.
3. Sanity check each quantity against the size of the site.

## Rates

* If house rates are given, use them.
* If only the round figure is given, you may derive rates so that the parts reproduce it, and say so. Do not introduce an amount the record and the house rules do not support.

## Settlement

Tell the customer how the final quantities will be agreed.
